significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that a conditional subliminal trait consists of "two dissociable early-layer directions" whose gating predicts repair survival through the measurable coupling between payload activity and erasure; this combines a nontrivial causal decomposition with a form-(iii) predictive relation rather than merely showing that a direction exists. It would establish both a phenomenon—conditional traits are "simultaneously stealthier and stickier"—and a mechanism, while fixing expectations about cross-trigger payload transfer, selective disarming with trigger detection retained, and when benign fine-tuning will erase a trait; this bears directly on the persistence demonstrated in Cloud et al.'s Subliminal Learning and Hubinger et al.'s Sleeper Agents. The negative branches are also informative: failure of H1 rules out the proposed low-dimensional detector/payload account in favor of entangled or distributed mechanisms, while failure of H2 establishes that conditional dormancy does not confer the claimed repair resistance. True and false outcomes are determinate, and the topic-substitution check passes: replacing these specific claims with merely "extend research on subliminal learning" would not justify this score.

reach.justification: The named handles are "activation-level, trigger-search audits" that probe for "a latent payload direction that is silent behaviorally" and the measurable "fraction of fine-tuning steps in which the payload direction was active" as a predictor of erasure. The audit is ex ante because it can flag a dormant conditional trait before behavior-only certification or shipment, giving auditors and deployers an action window rather than only explaining an observed failure afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a detector/payload separation, cross-trigger payload transfer, and an activity–erasure coupling, so more than a search procedure survives recalibration; however, its asserted scope remains the class of trigger-conditioned subliminal traits across triggers, carriers, and model families rather than models or modalities generally. The topic-substitution check passes because the transferable audit and dormancy-based predictor disappear when the claim-specific gating hypothesis is deleted.
